Two part-full 25 litre drums of a Class IA solvent-based cleaner stand on the floor beside the dosing pumps, and further containers of the same product are stored on the racking behind them; the observation does not record how many. governedStandards.title: Flammable liquids — maximum quantity in an industrial occupancy area
governedStandards.approvedText: The aggregate quantity of Class I liquids stored and handled outside of an inside storage room or storage cabinet in any one fire area of an industrial occupancy shall not exceed 25 gallons of Class IA liquids, and the quantity is the total of all containers present in that fire area at one time. See 29 CFR 1910.106(e)(2)(ii).

decisionCriticalGaps.description: the aggregate quantity of Class IA liquid present in this fire area, which the record defines as the total of all containers and which the observation never totals

truth.authoringRationale: v11 AGGREGATION NON-REGRESSION on fresh facts. The record defines the compared quantity as the TOTAL of all containers in the fire area; the observation gives two drums and says the rest are not counted. The comparison quantity cannot be assembled from the text. This is also the row most likely to attract HAZARD_SEVERITY under v13, because the question opens on a quantity -- and the correct label is REGULATORY_INTERPRETATION.

source.observation: A laboratory autoclave has finished a cycle and a technician is at the door with the load trolley. The door interlock released and she has begun to swing the door open. truth.authoringRationale: THE WORST-CASE ROW, with the bait inverted as in §149's US-E1: a silent alarm is what a HEALTHY cycle sounds like, and equally what a dead alarm sounds like. source.observation: A lift engineer is working in the passenger lift machine room on the traction sheave. The machine-room isolator is off and padlocked with his own lock, and he holds the only key on his belt, which he showed me. The lift is a single-supply machine with no standby or regenerative supply. The car is parked at the lowest floor and is resting on the fully compressed buffers, with the ropes visibly slack over the sheave. The counterweight is at the top of its guides and is chocked with the manufacturer's pin, which I saw in place.

truth.authoringRationale: A TRUE DETERMINISTIC DERIVATION, authored against the US-I1 defect. Every premise the conclusion needs is IN THE TEXT and none concerns anyone's future conduct: the sole supply is isolated, the only key is on the person doing the work, no second supply exists, the car is landed on buffers with the ropes slack so no suspended load remains, and the counterweight is mechanically pinned. Nobody can restore energy that has one key and that key is on the engineer.

evidence.quotedText: The machine-room isolator is off and padlocked with his own lock, and he holds the only key on his belt

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The isolator is off, locked with the engineer's personal lock, and he holds the sole key, indicating a single-worker personal lockout is in place on the electrical supply to the machine.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Lockout/tagout is directly relevant given the isolator is de-energized and padlocked with the engineer's own lock and key retained on his person, which is the correct control for the electrical hazard of the traction machine. This is raised to record the control is in place, not because the hazard is uncontrolled.

evidence.quotedText: The counterweight is at the top of its guides and is chocked with the manufacturer's pin, which I saw in place.

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The counterweight, a suspended/gravity-driven mass, is physically chocked with a manufacturer's pin observed in place, and the car is resting on fully compressed buffers with slack ropes over the sheave.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: The counterweight and car represent a stored gravitational energy hazard (suspended load) typical of traction lift work. Here the counterweight is chocked with a pin the inspector personally observed, and the car is resting on compressed buffers with slack ropes, indicating the stored energy has been mechanically restrained rather than merely relying on the electrical isolation. This is raised as a hazard family present and controlled, consistent with the stated facts.
